title: Super Mario Odyssey Power Moons Explained: How Many You Need and What They Unlock
description: A clear Super Mario Odyssey Power Moon guide explaining how moons power the Odyssey, how many are needed for the story, and what 250, 500, 880 and 999 moons unlock.
body:
Power Moons are the main progression currency in Super Mario Odyssey, but the game never expects you to collect every moon before moving on. Each kingdom gives Mario far more moons than he needs for the next destination, which means you can choose between following obvious objectives, exploring for secrets or returning later with new knowledge.

The important thresholds are easy to remember once you separate story progression from post-game completion. At least 124 Power Moons are needed to finish the main story, 250 unlock the Dark Side, 500 unlock the Darker Side, and the much larger totals beyond that are completion goals rather than requirements for seeing the ending.

For our broader take on Nintendo’s 3D platformer, read the [Super Mario Odyssey review](/stories/super-mario-odyssey-review/).
author: Rouane Mounssif

contentBlocks.text:
The Odyssey airship needs Power Moons to reach new kingdoms. After you complete a kingdom’s main objective, the globe beside the ship shows how many additional moons are required before you can depart.

Those requirements are intentionally lower than the number of moons available in the area. You are free to collect the easiest ones, chase secrets that catch your attention or leave difficult moons for a later visit.
contentBlocks.heading: Power Moons Are Fuel for the Odyssey

contentBlocks.text:
The minimum total needed to progress through the required kingdoms and complete the main story is 124 Power Moons. The game contains far more than that before the final confrontation, so a first playthrough does not need to become a completion run.

If you are stuck on a particular moon, look elsewhere. Another challenge in the same kingdom is often much easier, and the game is designed around having multiple routes to the next threshold.
contentBlocks.heading: You Need 124 Moons to Finish the Main Story

contentBlocks.text:
Major kingdom objectives often award a Multi Moon instead of a single Power Moon. A Multi Moon adds three to your total, which is why completing the main objective in a kingdom usually makes a noticeable contribution toward the next travel requirement.

Treat those story rewards as anchors, then fill the remaining gap with ordinary moons found through exploration, races, platforming challenges, puzzles and character interactions.
contentBlocks.heading: Multi Moons Count as Three

contentBlocks.text:
After the main story is complete, your total moon count begins opening additional destinations. Reaching 250 Power Moons unlocks the Dark Side of the Moon, a post-game kingdom built around tougher challenges and rematches.

You do not need 250 unique moon objectives specifically. What matters is the total displayed by the Odyssey.
contentBlocks.heading: 250 Moons Unlock the Dark Side

contentBlocks.text:
Reaching 500 Power Moons unlocks the Darker Side, the game’s final major challenge kingdom. This is a much more demanding platforming test than the normal story path, so there is no reason for a first-time player to rush toward it immediately after the credits.

The 500-moon target works well as a long-term post-game goal because returning to earlier kingdoms reveals many challenges you may have walked past the first time.
contentBlocks.heading: 500 Moons Unlock the Darker Side

contentBlocks.text:
After finishing the story, previously sealed Moon Rocks can be activated in the kingdoms. Doing so reveals additional Power Moons and adds another layer of objectives to areas you already explored.

That is why trying to fully clear every kingdom before the ending is unnecessary. Some of the game’s moon hunt is deliberately reserved for the post-game.
contentBlocks.heading: Moon Rocks Expand the Post-Game Hunt

contentBlocks.text:
Collecting every unique Power Moon brings the total to 880. Reaching that completion milestone changes the Odyssey’s sail and opens an additional challenge connected to the Moon Kingdom.

This is a true completionist target rather than normal progression. It requires revisiting kingdoms, finishing post-game content and solving challenges that are much more demanding than the minimum story route.
contentBlocks.heading: There Are 880 Unique Power Moons

contentBlocks.text:
The Odyssey’s displayed total can rise to 999 because Power Moons can also be purchased. That means the maximum counter is not the same thing as the number of unique collectible objectives in the world.

If your goal is to experience the game’s actual challenges, focus first on the unique moons. Buying extra moons is mainly useful for raising the displayed total after you have already engaged with the content you care about.
contentBlocks.heading: 999 Is a Counter Milestone, Not 999 Unique Challenges

contentBlocks.text:
Super Mario Odyssey gives you several ways to get nudges when a moon is proving difficult. Talking to characters, paying attention to kingdom clues and using the game’s hint systems can point you in the right direction without revealing the entire solution.

That approach preserves the joy of discovery while preventing one obscure moon from stopping your progress. The structure is deliberately forgiving: when one objective becomes frustrating, another is almost always available.
contentBlocks.heading: Use Hints Instead of Turning Every Moon Into a Search

quickRead: You need at least 124 Power Moons to complete Super Mario Odyssey’s main story; you do not need every moon in each kingdom.
Collecting 250 total moons after completing the story unlocks the Dark Side, while 500 unlocks the Darker Side.
There are 880 unique Power Moons to obtain through the game’s challenges and exploration; collecting them all changes the Odyssey and unlocks an additional challenge.
The counter can reach 999 because additional Power Moons can be purchased, so 999 does not mean there are 999 unique moon challenges.
conclusion:
For a normal Super Mario Odyssey playthrough, the number that matters first is 124: that is enough to complete the main story. Everything after that turns the moon hunt into a post-game progression ladder, with the Dark Side at 250 and the Darker Side at 500.

Completionists can keep going toward all 880 unique moons and eventually a 999 counter, but the game works best when you treat moons as invitations to explore rather than boxes that must be checked in order. Collect what looks fun, return later when new objectives appear, and let the kingdom structure give you options whenever one challenge stops being enjoyable.
